author: ojiudezue
title: The cycle that shipped nothing: six framing-disjoint reviews to find that guest mode's only safety check had never run
summary: A small guest/census correctness cycle (clamp the double-counting census, make guest rooms lead instead of the count) passed three framing-disjoint reviews, then its own fix-up introduced a HIGH, then an operator-ordered FOURTH-through-SIXTH pass found that the load-bearing identity check `_is_known_person_in_room` had never worked in production — two independent bugs in one 20-line helper, hidden behind a fail-open default. Nothing shipped. Three separate regressions were stopped: a false-guest-at-boot, a guest gate resting on a dead oracle, and a whole cycle of dedup work a 10-minute probe proved would buy zero. The night's durable output is process, not code: producer-AND-consumer checks, a third hollow-anchor variant, a pytest-serialization mechanism, and the lesson that agreement between two agents using the same wrong method reads exactly like verification.

decisions.decision: Separate census (measurement) from guest (policy state), with guest rooms leading and the count only corroborating.
decisions.why: Operator ruling: 'Census and guest are diff states... Census decay is also not the same as Guest decay. Separate concerns.' The house sat in `guest` for 7h02m with four known residents and zero guests; entry was census-driven (count hit 6, guest 30s later) and exit was blocked because the exit predicate required unidentified_count == 0. Guest was a function of a decaying measurement, which is the root architectural error, not a tuning problem.

decisions.decision: Use the Tier-3 fuller pass (adversarial completeness + lifecycle + test authority) even though three reviews had already returned SHIP.
decisions.why: Operator answered 'Fuller pass' when offered a single focused re-review. That call is the only reason the cycle did not ship. The three extra framings returned three DO-NOT-SHIPs. A focused pass scoped to the fix-up diff would have missed the dead oracle entirely, because the oracle predated the diff.

decisions.decision: Enforce pytest serialization as a PreToolUse hook rather than a prompt instruction.
decisions.why: The suite runs ~4 min alone and 30-45 min when overlapped; a 43-min straggler was found holding the host while three agents queued. A prompt rule cannot hold because parallel agents each individually believe they are the only one — there is no vantage point inside a single agent from which to see the contention. Mechanism over rule, same reasoning as the disposition-apply forcing function.

decisions.decision: Drop the census dedup repair on probe evidence instead of building it.
decisions.why: Measure-before-you-build: the probe showed BLE-cancel is not broken code at all. The kill switch is on and the map is non-empty; the break is area-set disjointness (3 of 7 camera areas have no URA room, and no interior camera covers any bedroom or bathroom - residents were in a camera-covered room for 3.75% of person-minutes all week). It is a coverage/config problem. Meanwhile 74.5% of elevated-census time had camera_unrecognized == 0 - pure hold/decay tail. The decay work is the high-value item; the dedup work was worth ~0.

decisions.decision: Merge the two census cycles and run three cycles in parallel after the operator flagged the pace as slow.
decisions.why: The complaint was fair. But the throughput problem was never the reviews - it was a 10x pytest tax and a fix-up that skipped its own producer check. Cycles 2 and 3 were both census-side and shared every consumer and test surface, so splitting them bought isolation nobody needed at the cost of a full review round.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Ship D1/D2b/D3 and hold only D2 (the guest composition change).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Operator: 'Don't hold the cycle.' Also moot once the designation error was corrected - with guest rooms genuinely designated, the dead oracle is a live bug that D2 makes load-bearing, so the oracle fix is a prerequisite either way rather than a follow-up.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Rename the 23 `_2`-suffixed Frigate face entities so the code's constructed slug resolves.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works today and re-breaks on the next collision. The durable fix is registry resolution, for which this very cycle already set precedent: D3 replaced constructed-slug lookup with entity_registry.async_get_entity_id for exactly this failure class.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Build exterior->guest admission alongside the exterior headcount swap.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Marginal-benefit decomposition. The headcount swap is read-only composition of a better number we already own; the admission path would create the FIRST exterior->house-state trust edge for ~5 minutes off a 30-minute dwell in a rare event. Parked with a revisit trigger, not deleted.

implications.implication: Bug Class #63 - dead oracle behind a fail-open default.
implications.detail: `_is_known_person_in_room` looked up `manager.coordinators.get('person')` (the person coordinator is never registered; all 7 sibling sites in the same file use hass.data[DOMAIN]['person_coordinator']) AND read `_tracked_persons` (one reference repo-wide: the read itself). It short-circuited on the first, masking the second, so a fix addressing only one would still have been silently broken. The `except -> return False` made it look defensive while being inert. Detection: for every attribute a predicate depends on, grep for its WRITERS; zero writers IS the finding. Odd-one-out is guilty until proven innocent.

implications.implication: Bug Class #64 - oracle-echo hollow anchor, a third variant beyond delete and comment-out.
implications.detail: A test computed its expected bound by importing the production constant it claimed to guard, so both sides moved together. Setting that constant to 0 - its own documented kill-switch value - left the test green. Attack by DETACHING the value, not by removing code.

D2 (guest rooms lead) and D3 (repair guest-room resolution) are each harmless alone and jointly dangerous: D3 activated a path that was partly dead, and D2 made that newly-live path the sole authority - over a helper that had never worked. When a change promotes a previously-OR'd path to sole authority, every helper on it must be re-verified as if newly written, even with a zero-line diff.

implications.implication: Two agents agreeing via one shared wrong method reads exactly like verification.
implications.detail: The builder reported 'no rooms designated is_guest_room'; I verified it - using the same wrong key. The real key is `room_is_guest_room`. Three rooms WERE designated, including a bathroom (misconfiguration, now unflagged), which made the dead oracle a live bug and likely explains the probe's otherwise-unexplained finding that 72% of guest minutes had unidentified_count == 0: Path B firing on residents with no census involvement. Verify the METHOD, not just the claim.

implications.implication: A reviewer's wrong diff base silently voids its entire framing.
implications.detail: Review B used two-dot `A..B` from the cycle's own first commit, which excludes A, so it concluded a whole deliverable was absent and declared its ripple analysis 'vacuous' - i.e. its assigned framing never ran, and it returned a confident SHIP. Caught only because a sibling framing had drilled the same code. Treat 'this framing turned out to be N/A' as a red flag requiring proof, and never inherit a reviewer's claim about branch CONTENTS.

commits: 7e3fa18d0 oracle fix (canonical lookup + real data shape + BLE-flap sticky latch)

revisit_trigger: If the repaired oracle's first organic guest visit does NOT arm GUEST (over-correction), or if a resident in a designated guest room still arms it (the phone-left-behind path, carded as GUEST-IDENTITY-PHONE-LEFT-BEHIND-1). Either outcome falsifies the fix in a way the suite cannot.
